label: late preregistration: written AFTER the first run's results (both arms 30/30) were seen
reason: Every statement text starts with its own dateline (e.g. 'September 18, 2024 Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement') and the query names the month and year, so the first run cannot show whether dense retrieval gets dates right from content. This ablation tests whether the probe can detect date errors.
expectation: With the dateline and any explicit full dates (Month DD, YYYY) removed from the indexed text, the dense arm's top-1 date correctness drops well below 1.0 (neighbouring meetings with similar wording), while the dense+date_filter arm stays at 1.0 because the date lives in the payload.
criteria: Same 30 sealed queries, same embedding endpoint, new collection g2amw_fomc_statements_nodate.
Remove every 'Month DD, YYYY' pattern and the 'For release at ... Share' header from the text before embedding; payload dates unchanged.
Report the same metrics for both arms; no further changes after seeing scores.
